texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Always round monetary values with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Raise BillingError with machine-readable codes Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors, using short snake_case codes like "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount"; mirror the pattern in ledgerly/payments.py authorize.
texts.at-0003: Normalize amounts through money helpers Convert any incoming amount with to_money() from ledgerly.money and compare against ZERO rather than raw numbers; never store unnormalized Decimals on models.
texts.at-0004: Reject bools when validating integers When validating an int argument, explicitly exclude bool (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since True/False pass isinstance(x, int).
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic; it rejects naive datetimes with a BillingError. Follow the pattern in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py:current_period`.
texts.at-0006: Compute periods via timedelta floor division Compute billing periods by building `length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` and using `(at - start) // length` for the period index, as in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py:current_period`; reuse this idiom instead of manual day math.

item.title: Use money helpers for all amounts
item.content: Convert every monetary input with `to_money` from `ledgerly.money` and round results with `round_money`; never do float arithmetic on amounts. `to_money` rejects floats with `BillingError("float_amount")`.
